records.issue_text: [BUG] JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) runs with no try/catch, so a corrupt or undecryptable backupCodes value throws an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of the 4xx the endpoint's contract promises. A user whose backupCodes column holds invalid ciphertext (or CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotated) hits a raw 500 on every disable attempt with no actionable error, while every other failure path on this endpoint returns a 400 with an ErrorCode.
records.rationale: In the new backup-code disable flow (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`), the code does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` with no surrounding try/catch. records.issue_text: [BUG] The verified backup code is nulled and persisted to the DB before the remainder of authorize() runs, so any later failure in authorize burns the code without granting a login. A user who submits a valid backup code but then trips a subsequent failure in authorize (e.g., an org/SSO check throwing) permanently loses that one-time code and receives only a generic login error — the code is consumed with no way to recover it, and there is no log of the consumption.

records.issue_text: [BUG] JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) is unguarded, so decrypt/parse failure throws mid-authorize and produces an internal next-auth error rather than the MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode 4xx-shaped errors the rest of the branch uses. Users with corrupt stored backup codes get a raw internal error on every login attempt, and the failure mode is indistinguishable from a server outage.
records.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` with no try/catch. If `symmetricDecrypt(...)` returns invalid JSON (corrupt data, wrong key, etc.) or throws, `authorize()` will throw an unhandled exception instead of the explicit `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` / `ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode` errors used elsewhere in the branch. This is a real failure mode introduced/exposed by the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Closing the dialog via ESC or the Dialog X at the DisplayBackupCodes step (onOpenChange path) skips resetState and onEnable, so the backup codes are persisted server-side but never shown again and no regeneration path exists. A user who starts typing/copying their codes and accidentally hits ESC loses all 10 backup codes permanently: the codes were stored at setup/enable time, there is no API to re-display or regenerate them (only full disable + re-enable, which itself now requires a working second factor), and the parent UI never learns 2FA was enabled. Silent data loss on a user-facing flow.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] navigator.clipboard.writeText is fire-and-forget: the success toast shows immediately without awaiting the promise, so a rejected write (insecure context, permission denied) is silently swallowed while the UI reports success. Users on non-HTTPS deployments or with clipboard permission revoked are told 'Backup codes copied!' when nothing was copied — and for one-time-use codes this is data loss, since the codes can never be re-displayed.
records.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal’s backup codes step, the Copy button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting/handling its returned promise, and immediately shows a success toast: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...); showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success");`. If the clipboard write rejects (e.g., insecure context or permission denied), the UI will still report success and the error is swallowed.

Users who open the enable-2FA flow repeatedly accumulate leaked object URLs/Blobs for the lifetime of the page; minor but unbounded across repeated toggling in one session.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Backup codes are generated and persisted at setup time (before the user ever completes the TOTP verification step), so each aborted-and-restarted setup silently discards previously issued codes and a user who saw codes from an earlier setup attempt (e.g., in a parallel tab) has those codes invalidated without any indication. Two concurrent setup sessions (two tabs, or setup then re-setup before enabling) overwrite each other's backup codes; the earlier-shown codes silently fail at login with IncorrectBackupCode and the user has no way to know which set is current.
